subject.title: config: use datetime suffix for config backup files instead of numeric rotation

question: Should timestamped config backups preserve or convert existing numbered `.bak.N` recovery points, or may the migration delete them when the suffix scheme changes?
rationale: Config backups can be the user's only rollback path, and the repository policy treats config migration and recovery behavior as upgrade-sensitive rather than an automation-only cleanup choice.

options.title: Preserve or convert legacy backups
options.body: Require this PR or a replacement to keep `.bak.N` recovery points until they are represented in the bounded timestamp retention set, with permission hardening and upgrade tests.

options.title: Accept timestamp-only cleanup
options.body: Allow first-run cleanup to delete numbered backups and document that maintainers are accepting the recovery-retention break on upgrade.

options.title: Pause the naming change
options.body: Keep the numeric ring for now and leave the timestamped naming request tracked by the canonical issue until a migration-safe design is approved.

recommendation.title: Preserve or convert legacy backups
recommendation.body: Require this PR or a replacement to keep `.bak.N` recovery points until they are represented in the bounded timestamp retention set, with permission hardening and upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent commit and merge history around backup cleanup, config write maintenance, and adjacent backup-rotation tests.
